## Findings
- claim-1: Let \(q=n-r\), \(R=i^j\), \(d=ij\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), and assume \(\min(i,j)=2\), \(\min(p,c)=1\). In the truncated Schur/Pieri presentation for shapes in the \(q^r\)-box containing \(R\), the columns and Pieri rows in degrees \(d+1,d+2\) are exactly those listed below; all boundary deletions are explicit.
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(R=i^j\), \(d=ij\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), with
\[
\min(i,j)=2,\qquad \min(p,c)=1.
\]
Thus \(i,j,p,c\ge1\), \(i,j\ge2\), and \(p=1\) or \(c=1\).

In the truncated Schur/Pieri presentation, the degree-\(d\) column is
\[
x_0=s_{i^j}.
\]

The complete degree-\(d+1\) column list is
\[
x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\qquad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)}.
\]
Both lie in the \(q^r\)-box since \(p,c\ge1\). The sole indexed Pieri row of this degree is
\[
(1)\qquad h_1x_0=x_1+y_1.
\]
There are no other rows: a positive-degree Pieri product reaching degree \(d+1\) must have source degree \(d\) and multiplier \(h_1\). On complementary column \(y_1\), row (1) has unit entry \(1\). Hence the degree-\(d+1\) quotient is freely generated by \(\bar x_1\), with \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\).

The complete degree-\(d+2\) column list is
\[
\begin{aligned}
u&=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})} &&\text{present iff }p\ge2,\\
x_2&=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\\
z&=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\\
y_2&=s_{(i^j,2)},\\
w&=s_{(i^j,1,1)} &&\text{present iff }c\ge2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The three complete indexed Pieri rows are
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2)\quad h_2x_0&=u+z+y_2,\\
(3)\quad h_1x_1&=u+x_2+z,\\
(4)\quad h_1y_1&=z+y_2+w,
\end{aligned}
\]
with absent \(u,w\) deleted. Completeness follows because a row landing in degree \(d+2\) has either source \(x_0\) and multiplier \(h_2\), or source \(x_1,y_1\) and multiplier \(h_1\).

The unit complementary minors are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(p,c)&\text{complementary columns}&\text{selected rows}&\det\\ \hline
(1,c),\ c\ge2 &(z,y_2,w)&(2),(3),(4)&
\det\!\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}=-1\\[1em]
(p,1),\ p\ge2 &(u,z,y_2)&(2),(3),(4)&
\det\!\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}=1.
\end{array}
\]
Thus in either non-corner boundary case all complementary columns are integrally eliminated, leaving \(\bar x_2\) freely.

For \((p,c)=(1,1)\), both \(u,w\) are absent. Retaining indexed rows, the full row array on \((x_2,z,y_2)\) is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1&1\\
1&1&0\\
0&1&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Rows (2) and (4) coincide. Selecting rows (2),(3) on complementary columns \((z,y_2)\) gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det=-1.
\]
The remaining row (4) equals row (2), so it supplies no residual relation on \(x_2\). Hence this degree quotient is again \(\mathbb Z\bar x_2\).

## Gaps
This certificate assumes the stipulated truncated Schur/Pieri presentation and concerns only
\[
\min(i,j)=2,\qquad \min(q-i,r-j)=1.
\]
It does not establish completeness in other parameter regimes or any global minimality statement.

## Next
The requested local certificate is established in the stated regime: the degree-\(d+1\) and degree-\(d+2\) columns and indexed Pieri rows are complete, including all boundary deletions and unit determinant witnesses.
